subject.title: [Feature]: Add runtime testing for skill workshop proposals before apply

question: What pre-apply execution boundary should Skill Workshop runtime validation use for pending skill proposals?
rationale: Running or simulating generated skill behavior before apply can cross approval, filesystem, tool-policy, and side-effect boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Stage load/schema validation first
options.body: Add a shared runtime-validation service that checks proposal load, registry discovery, and schema visibility, while deferring invocation until a safe oracle and side-effect model exists.

options.title: Allow sandboxed invocation now
options.body: Define proposal-provided or generated representative inputs plus strict sandbox/tool/network/filesystem limits before adding invoke and side-effect checks.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle-contract work
options.body: Track this only as part of the broader Skill Workshop lifecycle contract so one artifact owns validation semantics and apply readiness.

recommendation.title: Stage load/schema validation first
recommendation.body: Add a shared runtime-validation service that checks proposal load, registry discovery, and schema visibility, while deferring invocation until a safe oracle and side-effect model exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The Skill Workshop proposal store, CLI, and Gateway lifecycle all trace to shakkernerd's feature-introduction commits.
